p5_b1.ocr: Fig 4. Huber robust regression with lifetime substance use in occasional stimulant users (n = 158). Stimulant users with relatively greater lifetime stimulant uses show a diminished recruitment of anterior cingulate. Risky vs. safe decisions, cluster significance of p < .05 corrected for multiple comparisons (voxel-wise probability: p < .05). doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0127010.g004 absence of behavioral alterations at early stages of stimulant use suggests that cognitive impair- ments may increase with greater use of drugs [22, 68] as research has highlighted behavioral impairments in chronic users. Nevertheless, neural differences emerged between OSU and CS despite the absence of behavioral impairments in OSU, suggesting that OSU and CS differ in the process arriving at decisions. Specifically, OSU presented an attenuated neural differentia- tion of risky and safe decisions, thus seemed less sensitive to adverse consequences of risk tak- ing. This finding extends recent results of our group showing a blunted neural response to risk in the absence of performance differences to be indicative of relapse to stimulant use [50]. OSU displayed a pronounced attenuation of dorsal striatum, ACC, prefrontal and insular activation to both risky and safe decisions.
